Your repositories, your fonts, your git setup — and notifications when CI is done.

### Repositories already on your Mac

- The Welcome screen has an **On this Mac** tab: every repository in your code folders (found automatically the first time, e.g. `~/Code` or `~/Downloads/Code`), grouped by folder, with branch, uncommitted changes, ahead/behind and last activity.
- **Clone from GitHub** marks the repositories you already have and offers **Open** instead of cloning a second copy.
- Choose the folders in **Settings → General → Repository folders**.

### A much bigger Settings

- **Fonts**: interface and code font from the fonts installed on your machine, sizes, ligatures, tab width, and window zoom (⌘+ ⌘− ⌘0), with a live preview.
- **Git**: your global name and email, commit and tag signing (GPG, SSH or X.509) with your signing key — written to `~/.gitconfig`. Signed commits show **Verified** in the commit details.
- **Auto-stash**: uncommitted changes are stashed and put back when you switch branches or pull (on by default).
- **Commits & graph**: hide the author, date or SHA columns or tags; relative or absolute dates in your format, 12- or 24-hour; a subject-length guide for commit messages; a commit template (or git's own `commit.template`); skip hooks by default.
- **Diff & editor**: ignore whitespace at line ends (including CR) or everywhere.
- **External tools**: pick your editor (VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Sublime, Xcode… whatever is installed) — **Open in editor** is on file menus, the toolbar and ⌘K. **Open in diff tool** and **Open in merge tool** use the tools git finds (FileMerge, VS Code, Beyond Compare, Meld, KDiff3…).
- **Notifications**: a desktop notification when a CI run on your branch finishes, when a fetch brings new commits, or when a long push/pull/clone is done — and a check for a new version on startup.
- **Clone into**: a default folder for new clones.

### Fixes

- The scan waits for macOS's folder-access prompt and says so instead of looking stuck.
- Windows: editor detection and launching, and repository names from Windows paths.

### Install

Download the file for your system below. The builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet: on macOS right-click the app and choose **Open** the first time (or run `xattr -cr "/Applications/Git Graph.app"`); on Windows choose **More info → Run anyway**. Pull requests and Actions use the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) sign-in (`gh auth login`).
